title: The Sunken Chapel
author: You
description: A small d20 dungeon: the d20-lite preset with one stat changed and one added, two enemies at once, a boss with armor, and a fight against the clock.

ring.name: Drowned ring
ring.description: Cold, tight, and it will not come off. -3 Might.

tonic.name: Marsh tonic
tonic.description: +5 HP. Quick to drink: it does not cost your turn in a fight.

bandage.name: Bandage
bandage.description: +8 HP. Binding a wound in a fight costs the round.

steps.title: The steps
steps.text:
The marsh took the chapel a lifetime ago; only the bell tower still shows. You go down the tower steps into green half-light with a mace, a tonic and a bandage.

Might {might}, Agility {agility}, Faith {faith}, HP {hp}.

ring.title: The drowned ring
ring.text: Your fingers close on a ring, and the ring closes on your finger. Your arm goes heavy and cold (-3 Might while you wear it, and you will wear it).

font-blessing.title: Still water
font-blessing.text: The water in the font is clear and very still. You drink a handful, and feel watched over (+2 Faith).

nave.title: The nave
nave.text: Two shapes stand up out of the water between the pews: a robed thing with a candle snuffer, and a rat the size of a dog. They come at you together.

door.title: The crypt door
door.text: A bronze door, green with age, with a prayer cast into it and no handle.

choices.text: Say the prayer (1d20 + Faith, 12 or more)
Put your shoulder to it (1d20 + Might, 13 or more)

door-hurt.title: Bronze
door-hurt.text: The door does not move, and the cold of it goes through you (-2 HP).

crypt.title: The crypt
crypt.text: The abbot sits on his own tomb in rusted mail, holding the chapel bell-rope. The water is rising: you can hear it on the stairs. Finish this before it reaches the roof.

bell.title: The bell
bell.text: The abbot folds into the water. You take the rope from his hand and pull, and far above, for the first time in a lifetime, the chapel bell rings over the marsh.

flood.title: The flood
flood.text: The water is at your chest and the abbot is still standing. You swim for the stairs with your lungs burning. Behind you the crypt fills.

retreat.title: Daylight
retreat.text: You climb back up the tower into daylight, wet to the neck. The bell stays silent. Somebody braver, or luckier, may try next year.
